findings.title: [P1] Prevent escaped filenames from bypassing heredoc execution detection
findings.body:
The new scrubber can remove commands from a heredoc that is executed later in the same Bash invocation. For example: `cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/payload
if true; then rm -rf --no-preserve-root /; fi
EOF
bash /tmp/pay\load`. Bash resolves `pay\load` to `payload`, but `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` removes quotes without resolving backslash escapes, so it misses the execution. `_bdb_hd_scan_body` then drops the destructive command because its segment starts with `then`, leaving no `rm` for the normal fence rules to inspect. Canonicalize literal shell words before comparing destinations, and retain bodies whenever subsequent execution cannot be ruled out.

findings.failure_mode: The new scrubber can remove commands from a heredoc that is executed later in the same Bash invocation.

findings.cross_file_justification: The marker .run/implement-active.json is produced by `run-checkpoint.sh mark` (diff-touched, truncated) which the implementing SKILL.md files instruct the model to invoke via Bash; the sanction consumer is in the diff-touched implement-gate.sh.
findings.description: The new `sanctioned_marker` path grants an unconditional allow (even under `implement_gate.mode: deny`) whenever `.run/implement-active.json` holds `{skill: implement|bug, sprint: <token>, started_at: <2h}`. That file is model-authored: the model can run `run-checkpoint.sh mark` or simply `printf '{"skill":"implement","sprint":"x","started_at":"'$(date -u +%FT%TZ)'"}' > .run/implement-active.json` from the Bash tool. The hook only guards Write/Edit, so the trust-input ask on `.run/implement-active.json` (line 340) does not cover Bash writes. The same file's own header comment treats the model-authored `tool_input.active_skill` claim as tighten-only precisely because it is model-authored; the marker is the same trust class but is allowed to grant. Likewise, a Bash `rm .run/sprint-plan-state.json` degrades deny to ask (`unknown_position`).
findings.failure_mode: A model (or prompt-injected session) in deny mode writes a fresh marker once via Bash and then performs unlimited App Zone Write/Edit operations for two hours with no ask and no deny, each logged as a legitimate `allow sanctioned_marker` row. The 'fence' advertised in guard-origins.yaml is a self-service gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat the marker as tighten-only or bind it to something the model cannot forge: have `run-checkpoint.sh mark` be invoked only by a harness-side hook (e.g. the skill-start hook) and include an HMAC over {skill,sprint,started_at} keyed by a secret stored outside the repo/.run, verified here; alternatively, in deny mode require BOTH a fresh derived RUNNING cache AND the marker, and never let the marker alone flip deny to allow. Also extend block-destructive-bash (or a Bash PreToolUse hook) to ask on shell redirections into `.run/implement-active.json` and the other trust inputs.

findings.description: `LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=1` in the hook's environment sanctions every App Zone write in every mode including deny. block-destructive-bash.sh (same PR) explicitly states the opposite principle for its fence: 'an environment variable can never switch the fence off'. Hook environment can be influenced by repo-controlled files loaded before Claude Code starts (direnv `.envrc`, shell rc files, `.claude/settings*.json` `env` blocks), several of which the heredoc classifier itself treats as executable content.
findings.failure_mode: Any mechanism that injects one env var into the Claude Code process (repo .envrc, settings env block, CI runner config) silently disables the deny fence for the whole session; the only trace is an `allow override` audit row that the model can also append to.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the env override for deny mode, or require it to be paired with an operator-only artifact outside the repo (e.g. a file under $HOME with mode 0600 whose owner is the invoking user), and emit the override row to the signed audit_emit chain rather than the plain hook log.

findings.cross_file_justification: profiles.yaml (new) defines the default; danger-level-enforcer.sh and input_guardrails.md (both diff-touched) now read the knob through profile-lib.sh instead of their previous `// true` / 'skip only if explicitly false' defaults.
findings.description: Two security guardrails flip from default-on to default-off. `is_enforcement_enabled()` previously returned true when the key was unset and when `.loa.config.yaml` was absent; it now returns `loa_knob guardrails.danger_level.enforce false`, which resolves to `false` under the default `standard` profile (and `lean`). `input_guardrails.md` previously ran unless explicitly disabled; it now runs only if the knob prints `true`, which `standard` does not. In addition, `source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/profile-lib.sh"` is unconditional with no error handling: if the lib is missing or `loa_knob` fails, `enforce` is empty and enforcement is off (fail-open).
findings.failure_mode: Every deployment that has not explicitly set these keys (i.e. all existing installs that relied on the old default) silently loses danger-level enforcement and pre-execution input guardrails after upgrade. A missing/broken profile-lib.sh also disables enforcement without any visible error.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep security-relevant keys default-on in `standard` (or exclude them from profile control entirely and read them with an explicit `true` fallback), add them to the floor list if they are meant to be floors, and make the enforcer fail-closed: `source ... || { log; return 0 /*enabled*/ }` and treat an empty knob result as `true`. Call out the default flip prominently in the migration notes.

findings.description: The classifier decides a heredoc body is 'nonexec' and drops non-fence-verb segments when the write target is not detected as executed in the same command. `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` requires the target's literal basename to appear as a token after quote-stripping; a glob (`bash t*`, `. ./pay?oad`), brace expansion, or `${var}` built path (`bash "${PWD}/${n}"`) that resolves to the file is not matched, so the body is still scrubbed. `_bdb_hd_exec_dest` resolves relative targets against the hook process's `$PWD`, ignoring a `cd /usr/local/bin &&` in the same command, so a write into a PATH or bin directory is judged non-executable. Line numbers are approximate; the symbol anchor is authoritative.
findings.failure_mode: `cd /usr/local/bin && cat <<'EOF' > t` + body + `bash t*` executes a model-written script in one Bash call while the fence sees only the header and fence-verb lines; body content that the main rules match by pattern rather than by one of the listed verbs (redirect to a block device, chmod/chown sweeps, fork bomb, curl|sh inside a quoted string) is no longer scanned. Impact is tempered by the documented gap that the Write tool is unfenced, but this is an in-command bypass, which the design claims to cover.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat any later segment whose first word is an interpreter/`.`/`source`/`exec`/`chmod` and whose argument contains a glob, brace, or expansion as 'may execute the target' (fail closed to interpreter). Resolve relative destinations against the cwd implied by a preceding `cd` in the same command, or classify any command containing `cd` before the heredoc header as interpreter. Add corpus cases for `bash t*`, `cd <bin> && cat <<EOF > t`, and `${var}` paths.

findings.description: Under the default `heredoc_classifier: true`, a 'nonexec' heredoc body is reduced to only those segments whose command word is in this hardcoded list (rm git find dd shred truncate kubectl terraform aws gcloud psql mysql mkfs* DROP DELETE TRUNCATE). The main fence's rule set is maintained separately (`_bdb_re_git`, `_bdb_re_brbd`, and the rest of the file not shown); any rule keyed on a verb absent here (e.g. `br`/`bd` delete, `gh repo delete`, `chmod`, `chown`, `mv`, `crontab -r`, device redirects, fork bomb) is silently excluded from heredoc bodies. The quote-stripping in `_bdb_hd_segword` also yields `r` for `'r'm -rf /`, so a trivially quoted verb is dropped before the fence rules ever see it. Nothing ties this allow-list to the rule set, so future rule additions will not propagate.
findings.failure_mode: Rules added to the main fence are not applied inside nonexec heredoc bodies, and the divergence is invisible until a corpus case fails. A body like `'r'm -rf "$HOME"` written to a file and later executed is never kept for the rules.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the fence-verb set from the same source as the main rules (a single array used by both), or keep the full body in the scrub copy and instead suppress only the specific #1245 false-positive pattern. At minimum, make `_bdb_hd_segword` fall back to 'full scan' when the command word contains quotes, backslashes, or ANSI-C `$'` quoting rather than truncating at the first quote. Add lint (tools/check-knob-readers.sh style) that fails when a verb matched by the main rules is missing here.

findings.cross_file_justification: constraints.json deletes C-TEAM-001..005 and the regenerated CLAUDE.loa.md drops the whole 'Agent Teams' table; whether the mechanical enforcers they named (`team-skill-guard.sh`, the PreToolUse Write/Edit System Zone hook) were also removed lives in agent-teams-reference.md / hooks-reference.md, which are truncated from this diff.
findings.description: All five agent-team constraints are removed, including C-TEAM-005 (teammates MUST NOT modify `.claude/`, 'enforced by PreToolUse:Write/Edit hook', severity critical, incident bridgebuilder-horizon-pr341) and C-TEAM-002/003/004 (lead-only beads, .run state, and git commit/push). The constraint text was the prompt-layer control that told teammates not to rewrite hooks, constraints, or settings for every agent in a team. No replacement constraint appears in the diff, and the implement-gate rows show `LOA_TEAM_MEMBER` is still a live role, so teammates still exist.
findings.failure_mode: If the hook enforcement was removed alongside the constraint (cannot be verified here), a teammate agent can edit `.claude/hooks/*`, `.claude/settings.json`, or constraints.json and alter the fence/gate behaviour for the lead and all other teammates, which is exactly the incident that produced C-TEAM-005. If the hook remains, the removal still deletes the recorded rationale and source incident without a pointer to where the rule now lives.
findings.suggested_fix: If agent teams are being retired, remove the `LOA_TEAM_MEMBER` branches and document the retirement in the reference. Otherwise keep C-TEAM-005 (and 002/003/004) in constraints.json or move them into a surviving section with the same `source_incident`, and confirm in hooks-reference.md that the PreToolUse Write/Edit System Zone guard and team-skill-guard.sh are still registered.

findings.description: `position_state` is taken from `.state // .status` of `.run/sprint-plan-state.json`, control-stripped but not length-limited, then interpolated into the stderr line and the `permissionDecisionReason` JSON returned to the harness via `deny_reason`. Every other untrusted string this hook emits (file_path, active_skill) is cut to 256 bytes per the sprint-250 audit notes; this new one is not.
findings.failure_mode: A multi-megabyte `state` string in a Bash-written cache bloats the hook's stderr and the deny payload shown to the user, and can be used to push arbitrary text into the permission prompt.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply `cut_utf8_256` to `position_state` as done for `audit_file_path`, and restrict it to a known vocabulary (RUNNING|HALTED|COMPLETE|unknown) before display.
